newsitem.title: USA: Mitchell Energy sees higher prices, output.
newsitem.headline: Mitchell Energy sees higher prices, output.

text.p: Mitchell Energy & Development Corp reported a drop in first first quarter earnings, saying energy prices have rebounded in the second quarter and the company expects to increase production.
The company said it earned $16.5 million, or $0.32 a share, in the quarter ended April 30, compared with net $23.2 million, or $0.45 a share, a year earlier.
Excluding unusual items in both years, the company earned $19.3 million, or $0.37 a share, versus $18.7 million, or $0.36 a share, in the same period last year.

"Operating results were very good in the first quarter, despite the impact of softer energy prices in March and April and unusually wet weather, which slowed both our drilling schedule and residential lot sales pace," said chief executive George P. Mitchell.
"Energy prices have rebounded in the second quarter, and we expect to increase our oil and gas production, as we catch up on well completions that were delayed by the rain.

"In real estate, while we did not match the record residential lot sales set in last year's first quarter, activity still was very strong. We sold 309 lots in the first quarter, and we're off to a good start toward our target of 1,250 for the year," Mitchell said.

Unusual items in the latest quarter included a $7 million provision for North Texas water well litigation costs. As the company said Wednesday, a Wise County jury found in favor of Mitchell on all counts in the "Bailey" case, involving 17 plaintiff groups. A three-judge appeals panel in Fort Worth is still deliberating over the company's appeal of the earlier "Bartlett" case involving eight plaintiff groups. A decision is expected in the next several months.
